transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came because after nights when I eat like that, I’m left sitting there with crumbs and empty containers everywhere, just feeling ashamed and disgusted with myself. The next morning I can hardly pray or look the people at church in the eye.
During those nights, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?
Yes. On a bad night, I might start with some leftover casserole, and then I’ve eaten that, half a pan of brownies, biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is in the refrigerator—all in one sitting.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself vomit afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything else to try to prevent weight gain, such as using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?
I’m not sure what you mean by trying to prevent weight gain. I don’t really know what I’m supposed to do after it happens.
When those eating episodes are happening, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you eat?
Yes. Once I take that first bite after the house is quiet, it’s like my good sense just steps aside. I’m telling myself, “Belinda, stop now,” but I keep reaching for more anyway.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I mean, I don’t think about my weight or shape all that much when I’m judging myself.
How often do these nights of uncontrollable eating happen?
Since my friend passed, it’s been at least once or twice most weeks. There hasn’t really been a month where it eased up.
Since your friend passed away, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not really sure. It’s been a hard time, of course, but I couldn’t say whether I’ve felt depressed most days.
Do these episodes of overeating cause you a lot of distress?

Yes, very much. Afterward I’m sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, just ashamed and disgusted with myself. I can hardly pray, and I don’t even want to look people at church in the eye the next morning.
During those nights, do you eat much faster than you normally would?
Yes. I stand at the kitchen counter and eat so fast I barely taste the pound cake or crackers. Sometimes I realize I’ve swallowed before I’ve even properly chewed.
During those episodes, do you keep eating even when you aren’t physically hungry?
I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t really stop to notice whether I’m hungry or not when it starts.
During those episodes, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
Yes. I keep going until my stomach feels tight and sore under my nightgown. Then I have to ease myself into the recliner because it hurts to move around.
During these eating episodes, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you’re eating?

Yes. At bridge or church suppers, I make a point of taking just a modest little plate. But later, after everyone’s gone home, I’ll pull out the leftovers and eat in the kitchen where nobody can see me.
When these eating episodes begin, do you feel sad?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed feeling sad right when it begins.
During those episodes, do you eat even when you are not physically hungry?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m hungry when it starts.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed feeling down most of the day like that.
During those episodes, do you eat even when you are not physically hungry?
I really can’t say for sure. I don’t usually stop and check whether I’m physically hungry when it happens.
On those nights when this happens, do you start eating even though you are not physically hungry?
I honestly don’t know. I don’t really pay attention to whether I’m hungry before I start eating.
Do these episodes of uncontrollable eating upset you a great deal?

Yes, very much. Afterward I’m sitting there with crumbs and empty containers around me, and I just feel ashamed and disgusted with myself. I can hardly pray or look people at church in the eye the next morning.
